problems.title: The learnable geometric proximity scorer has no differentiable route to the task loss
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF pp. 4–5; Appendix Algorithm 1, PDF p. 23.
claim: Section 3.3, PDF pp. 4–5, and Algorithm 1, PDF p. 23, describe a learnable proximity score followed by selecting the \(K^g\) smallest-score entities and aggregating their features. Released models/geo_group.py, TransformerBlock.forward, uses the box_pos linear scorer only to produce top-k indices for gathering those entities.
analysis: The scorer values affect the task loss only through discrete neighbor indices and are then discarded. That index-selection operation provides no differentiable path to the scorer. Including the scorer in an optimizer cannot create a missing gradient route; learning it requires an additional continuous dependence or separate objective.
result: The declared proximity scorer cannot learn through discarded integer top-k indices; other group-context and detector parameters can still learn.
repair: Either describe the scorer as fixed, or add a differentiable score-value route or separate learning objective. One existing proposal subtracts \(s_{ij}/\tau\) from selected-neighbor attention logits; a shared scorer bias cancels in that softmax, so use an identifiable parameterization. This changes the architecture and does not differentiate membership changes or establish restored mAP.
problems.impact_rationale: The declared proximity scorer cannot learn through discarded integer top-k indices; other group-context and detector parameters can still learn.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing local or architectural proposal remains applicable to the unchanged current-head source; no author adoption or corrected model performance is established.

problems.title: The geometric overlap feature uses enclosing-box area rather than union area
claim: Paraphrase: Section 3.3, page 5, defines the overlap feature as
analysis: Two squares of side \(1/2\), offset by \((1/4,1/4)\), have intersection area \(1/16\) and union area \(7/16\), so their IoU is \(1/7\). Their enclosing rectangle has area \(9/16\), giving the released ratio approximately \(1/9\). The enclosing-box denominator differs from the union before any small stabilizing constant is considered.
result: The overlap feature is not IoU on valid boxes, while a separate correct author IoU utility limits the defect to this local feature.
repair: Use set union \(|B_i|+|B_j|-|B_i\cap B_j|\), or reuse the correct author IoU utility; define degenerate-box handling separately.
problems.impact_rationale: The overlap feature is not IoU on valid boxes, while a separate correct author IoU utility limits the defect to this local feature.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing local or architectural proposal remains applicable to the unchanged current-head source; no author adoption or corrected model performance is established.

problems.title: Semantic neighbor selection computes Euclidean rather than cosine neighborhoods
problems.source_location: Section 3.4, PDF p. 5; Appendix Algorithm 2, also labeled Algorithm S2 in the separate supplement.
claim: Section 3.4, PDF p. 5, and Appendix Algorithm 2 define semantic neighbors by cosine similarity. Released models/sem_group.py, knn, instead ranks Euclidean distances without the unit-norm restriction that would make these rankings equivalent.
analysis: From query \((1,0)\), candidate \((10,0.1)\) has cosine approximately \(0.99995\) but squared distance \(81.01\). Candidate \((1,1)\) has cosine approximately \(0.7071\) and squared distance \(1\). The neighbor order reverses even when self-neighbors are handled consistently.
result: Unnormalized Euclidean KNN can select different context from cosine similarity; no measured downstream detection effect is established.
repair: Compute cosine scores directly, or L2-normalize nonzero query features before the Euclidean KNN call; define the zero-vector and positional-feature conventions explicitly.
problems.impact_rationale: Unnormalized Euclidean KNN can select different context from cosine similarity; no measured downstream detection effect is established.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing local or architectural proposal remains applicable to the unchanged current-head source; no author adoption or corrected model performance is established.

problems.title: Released neighborhood settings disagree with the paper, and a constructor argument is ignored
problems.source_location: Section 3.5, PDF p. 6; Table 4(b,c), PDF p. 8.
claim: Section 3.5, PDF p. 6, and Table 4(b,c), PDF p. 8, specify geometric and semantic group sizes \(4\) and \(2\). The released GEN construction instead calls default Geometric_Group instances whose internal TransformerBlock uses \(2\), and a default Semantic_Group using \(4\). The inspected construction path supplies no override linking those settings to the paper's chosen pair.
analysis: The current GEN constructs default Geometric_Group objects whose internal block is hardcoded to \(k=2\); its semantic groups default to \(k=4\). The paper’s selected counts are \(K^g=4\), \(K^s=2\). Even passing geometric \(k=4\) does not reach the internal block. The constructor likewise stores num_layers without constructing that many internal blocks; this is distinct from GEN’s external stage loop and does not establish how the paper’s depth ablation was run.
result: The default neighbor counts and ignored constructor arguments impair reconstruction of the stated settings; publication checkpoint configuration is not established.
repair: Pass the requested neighbor count to the operational block and explicitly set the intended geometric/semantic counts at construction. Clarify whether depth means internal repeated blocks or external GEN stages, without inventing a new unvalidated composition.
problems.impact_rationale: The default neighbor counts and ignored constructor arguments impair reconstruction of the stated settings; publication checkpoint configuration is not established.
